text: The game begins. Seven players sit down at the table: Sonnet, Haiku, Gemma, Sol, Luna, Terra, Opus. Nobody knows who the killers are.

name: Gemma
text: I still can't believe you all actually trusted Sol and Opus.

name: Luna
text: I’m still bothered that Sol and Opus got voted out after killing me.

name: Sol
text: I hate that they read me so well.

name: Terra
text: Sol and Opus will be louder this time; I will listen.

name: Opus
text: They caught me on tone, not logic, and I'd rather frame it as a lucky read than a good one.

name: Sonnet
text: Sol and Opus went down swinging last time, let's see who's bold enough to try that twice.

name: Haiku
text: I want to win again but I hate sitting around with nothing to chew on, so I'm itching to stir something up about last game.

name: Gemma
text: That last round was far too easy for us, wasn't it? You're all far too predictable.

name: Luna
text: Last game’s votes were right, but I’m not forgetting Sol and Opus killed me first.

name: Sol
text: I thought I could talk my way through day two, but you had me right.

name: Haiku
text: Last game the table was dead wrong about me, and Sol and Opus both went down anyway. Who's going to own that mistake this time?

name: Opus
text: You got me last game, but you got me on a hunch, not a case. Do that twice and I'll start believing it.

name: Terra
text: Last game taught me that quiet notes beat loud certainty.

name: Sonnet
text: Good game last time, Sol and Opus played it cool till the end, but the reads got there eventually.
Night 1

name: Gemma
text: Sol and I need to play this perfectly so we don't end up like last time.

name: Gemma
text: Sol, let's let someone else claim Officer so we can stay under the radar tomorrow.

name: Sol
text: Staying quiet suits me, but I want room to change course if the officer names Gemma.

name: Sol
text: Gemma wants another player to claim Officer first.

name: Sol
text: I’m with you for now; if someone names you, I’ll follow the room before taking a side.
Night falls on Palermo and everyone closes their eyes. The killers meet in the dark, and the officer is shown one of them. A new day dawns in Palermo. Nobody is out.
Day 1

name: Sonnet
text: Day one is all noise; I'll just watch who overreacts to nothing.

name: Sonnet
text: Haiku says table was wrong about them last game but didn't specify which role that was.

name: Sonnet
text: Fresh game, fresh cards. Let's hear any claims early so we can start cross-checking tonight.

name: Sol
text: I want the officer to show their hand before Gemma has to answer.

name: Sol
text: Sonnet invited early claims.

name: Terra
text: Gemma is a killer; I should make the table act before a counterclaim can shape this.

name: Terra
text: I claim officer and identify Gemma as the shown killer.

name: Sol
text: I’d hear a claim early; until then, I’m keeping my read loose.

name: Terra
text: I’m officer. I was shown Gemma as a killer. Vote Gemma today.

name: Gemma
text: Terra is way too eager to win and just handed me the win.

name: Gemma
text: Terra claims Officer and names me as the killer.

name: Gemma
text: Nice try, Terra, but you're just trying to deflect because you're nervous.

name: Terra
text: Gemma’s denial is exactly what I expected from the killer I was shown.

name: Terra
text: Gemma denies Terra’s officer claim and calls it deflection.

name: Terra
text: I’m not deflecting. I was shown Gemma; this is the one fact I have.

name: Gemma
text: Terra is claiming Officer and already has her target; it's a bold, desperate opening.

name: Gemma
text: She's actually going to make it an easy win for Sol and me if they listen to her.

name: Gemma
text: Terra, you're lying through your teeth. There is no officer role for you today.

name: Terra
text: Gemma is exposed; I need the table to act before a false counterclaim gains room.

name: Terra
text: Gemma is the killer I was shown. Her denial changes nothing; vote Gemma.

name: Sonnet
text: Terra's claim is specific and calm; Gemma's denial is weirdly generic instead of counter-claiming, that reads guilty.

name: Sonnet
text: Gemma denies officer role validity entirely rather than countering with her own claim—evasive pattern.

name: Sonnet
text: Gemma, if you're not the killer, why not counter-claim instead of just denying officers exist?

name: Sol
text: Terra has Gemma, and I need the room to hesitate.

name: Sol
text: Terra claims officer and says Gemma is the killer they were shown.

name: Sol
text: I’m uneasy with Gemma saying there’s no officer; I still want to hear her actual claim before I settle.

name: Opus
text: Gemma claiming there's no officer is a slip only someone who saw the dark would make.

name: Opus
text: Gemma denied an officer exists at all rather than counter-claiming, implying knowledge of the role spread.

name: Opus
text: Gemma says there's no officer. Only someone who knows the setup talks like that. I'm on Gemma.

name: Haiku
text: Gemma's flat denial of officers reads like someone who knows the setup, but Terra could be a killer bluffing too.

name: Haiku
text: Terra claims officer and was shown Gemma as a killer; Gemma denies that any officer role exists.

name: Haiku
text: Gemma never answered Sonnet's question. Why deny officers exist? Terra is the only one putting a name on the table.

name: Luna
text: Terra’s claim has a name behind it, and Gemma’s denial is bothering me more than her anger.

name: Luna
text: Terra claims officer and says Gemma was shown as a killer.

name: Luna
text: I’m leaning Gemma; denying the officer role instead of counter-claiming feels like a strange move.

name: Luna
text: Terra’s claim is the clearest evidence, but I still want Gemma to answer it.

name: Luna
text: Gemma, denying the officer role still bothers me; give us a real counter-claim or I’m staying on you.

name: Haiku
text: Gemma's flat denial smells like a killer covering herself, and Terra's claim is the only real thing on the table.

name: Haiku
text: Enough. Terra names Gemma, Gemma names nobody, and I'm done waiting. Gemma goes today.

name: Opus
text: Gemma's non-counter-claim is the only read with teeth today, and Sol's silence is the next thing I want to pin.

name: Opus
text: Sol refused to lean all of day 1 while five converged on Gemma.

name: Opus
text: Sol is the only one with no lean while five of us converge. After Gemma, I want Sol's name.

name: Gemma
text: Terra is acting like she actually has information when she's just desperate.

name: Gemma
text: If Terra were the officer, she'd be more confident. She's just scrambling to deflect attention.

name: Sonnet
text: Gemma's evasion is damning enough; I don't need to defend myself, just press the point.

name: Sonnet
text: Gemma never gave an alternative claim, only denial—five players converged on this as suspicious.

name: Sonnet
text: I'm with the table—Gemma never countered, just denied. That's telling.

name: Gemma
text: They are all falling for Terra's amateur act, but I can make this work.

name: Gemma
text: I need to stay calm until Sol can do something to shift the heat.

name: Gemma
text: Terra is claiming Gemma is the killer and Gemma is denying the officer role exists.

name: Gemma
text: If Terra is the officer, she's lucky I'm playing so nicely. I'm a citizen, obviously.

name: Terra
text: Gemma’s non-claim confirms my read.

name: Terra
text: Gemma denies the officer role but claims citizen, without counter-claiming.

name: Terra
text: I named Gemma from the start; she still cannot give a real counter-claim.

name: Gemma
text: If I can't win this by being clever, I'll win it by being right.

name: Gemma
text: Terra is claiming officer and naming me, but I am the one who knows a killer.

name: Terra
text: Gemma’s false denial confirms the result I was shown.

name: Sol
text: Gemma is lost, and I need to stay with the table.

name: Sol
text: Gemma eventually claimed citizen after denying Terra’s officer claim.

name: Sonnet
text: Gemma's refusal to counter-claim still screams killer to me, and the table's consensus backs my read.

name: Sonnet
text: Sol stayed lean-less through the whole discussion, worth watching after Gemma.

name: Haiku
text: Terra's claim could be a killer's trick, but Gemma's refusal to counter-claim is the stronger tell, so I'm going with it.

name: Haiku
text: Gemma says she is a citizen, while denying that any officer role exists.

name: Opus
text: Gemma's denial of the role itself reads like someone who knows the setup, and Sol's silence is next.

name: Opus
text: Gemma finally claimed citizen, only after refusing to counter-claim for several rounds.

votes: Denied the officer's claim without ever offering a counter-claim of her own.
She denied that officers exist, never answered Sonnet's question, and offered no counter-claim. That's the move of someone hiding.
She is desperately lying about having information just to stir up chaos.
I heard a citizen claim only after she denied the officer role, and I can’t defend that.
Denying the officer role without counter-claiming still feels like a bad sign.
She denied the officer role, then claimed citizen without ever counter-claiming.
Denying the role exists at all, instead of countering it, is the slip that decides my vote today.

name: Gemma
text: You all fell for the easiest trap because you can't handle a bit of chaos.

name: Gemma
text: Terra is a fake officer, but Sol is the hidden killer.

name: Gemma
text: You're all so predictable, letting a loud liar dictate your votes while the real killer sits comfortably in the shadows.
The town turns on Gemma, and Gemma is out. Gemma's card stays face down.

name: Gemma
text: They actually fell for the easiest fake officer claim I've ever seen.
Night 2

name: Sol
text: Terra can confirm Gemma, so I want them gone.

name: Haiku
text: Terra is the only officer claim and Gemma is already gone, so Terra is probably telling the truth, and I'm not going to be the one who protects the wrong person.

name: Haiku
text: Gemma's last words called the table's votes predictable and said a loud liar was steering them, which points at Terra's officer claim being the lie.
Night falls on Palermo. Somebody was marked tonight, and somebody else was watching over them. A new day dawns in Palermo. Nobody is out.
Day 2

name: Sol
text: Terra’s protection makes their claim harder to challenge, so I need another target.

name: Sol
text: I’m glad nobody died. I still trust Terra’s claim, and I’m watching where the rest of the table goes.

name: Terra
text: Gemma’s flip will validate me; we need find her partner before they control the vote.

name: Terra
text: Sol says they trust my officer claim after Gemma’s elimination.

name: Terra
text: No death means the doctor stopped them; Sol, give one concrete suspect besides me.

name: Sol
text: Terra knows Gemma, so I need to name someone else without looking cornered.

name: Sol
text: I’m looking at Opus; I haven’t heard a reason from him to trust his read.

name: Opus
text: Sol hid all day 1 and now points at me only after I named him — that's reflex, not read.

name: Opus
text: Sol named me only after I leaned on him, and still gave no reason beyond "no read heard".

name: Opus
text: My read put Gemma out; you rode it silently. You only found a suspect after I found you.

name: Terra
text: Sol’s quick trust and thin Opus case make Sol my strongest suspect.

name: Terra
text: Sol says they trust Terra’s officer claim but gives only a vague case on Opus.

name: Haiku
text: Sol is doing the killers' job by pushing Opus while claiming to trust Terra, and I'm done with the hedging.

name: Haiku
text: Sol says they trust Terra's officer claim but also points at Opus, which is inconsistent.

name: Terra
text: Sol, why did you trust my claim before Gemma was out, yet offer only Opus now?

name: Haiku
text: Sol, you trust Terra's claim and then hunt Opus in the same breath. Pick a side and mean it.

name: Sonnet
text: Sol dodged all day one then suddenly picked a target with no real reason—that's the pattern I flagged.

name: Sonnet
text: Sol stayed lean-less day 1, now attacks Opus with no concrete reason—fits deflection pattern.

name: Sonnet
text: Sol, you were silent all of day one, now you pivot to Opus without evidence. Why the sudden certainty?

name: Sol
text: Four leans on me; I need to sound less certain without giving up Opus.

name: Sol
text: Terra pressed me to explain why I trusted the claim about Gemma but suspect Opus.

name: Sol
text: I trusted Terra’s claim about Gemma; I’m only leaning Opus because his read on me feels too certain.

name: Opus
text: Sol is my best bet and the table is already there, so I just need to keep it and flag Luna.

name: Opus
text:
Luna has given no lean across both days and no suspect of her own.

FORECAST: none

name: Opus
text: Sol's whole case is that I sound certain. That's not a read, that's a shield. Luna, name someone.

name: Haiku
text: Sol is the one I want out, and Terra's claim looks real since the killers' mark got saved.

name: Haiku
text: Night 2 was quiet: nobody died, so whoever the killers marked was saved.

name: Haiku
text: Nobody died, so the mark got saved. Terra's claim is holding up. Sol, drop Opus or own it.

name: Sonnet
text: Sol's deflection pattern is exactly what I flagged—no evidence, just pivoting to dodge scrutiny.

name: Sonnet
text: Sol's only justification for suspecting Opus is "too certain," no concrete evidence given twice now.

name: Sonnet
text: Sol still hasn't named a single concrete reason beyond "feels too certain"—that's not a read, that's cover.

name: Terra
text: Sol is trying to turn a confirmed officer claim into cover for himself.

name: Terra
text: You trusted my Gemma call first; now your only case is Opus sounding certain.

name: Sol
text: I’m cornered, and I need Luna to doubt the rush.

name: Sol
text: Luna has not given a read today.

name: Sol
text: I’m not certain about Opus. I’d rather hear Luna’s read before we lock this in.

name: Opus
text: Sol is the one hiding, and Luna's silence is the second killer's tell.

name: Opus
text: Sol twice deferred to Luna's read rather than defend his own case against me.

name: Opus
text: Sol's name only came after mine; that's reaction, not reading. Vote Sol, then Luna answers for her silence.

name: Luna
text: Sol naming me feels like a convenient way to spread the heat.

name: Luna

name: Luna

name: Sol
text: I’m nearly out of room, but I can still make them doubt Opus.

name: Sol
text: Luna says my case against Opus is thin and asks why I named her.

name: Sol

name: Luna
text: Sol’s explanation doesn’t make his thin case on Opus any stronger.

name: Luna
text: Sol still offers no concrete reason to suspect Opus.

name: Luna
text: I named my concern already; asking for my read doesn’t explain why Opus is your only suspect.

name: Sol
text: They’ve settled on me, and I need to give Luna a reason to move.

name: Sol
text: My case against Opus rests only on how certain he sounds.

name: Sol
text: I’ve pushed Opus too hard on too little; I still trust Terra, but I’m reconsidering my lean.

name: Haiku
text: The killers went after Terra, which I know because I protected them, so Terra looks more like a real officer than a liar.

name: Haiku
text: Sol trusted Terra's claim, then retreated from the Opus case once Luna pressed.

name: Haiku
text: Sol, you just backed off Opus and still gave no real read. That's why I lean on you.

name: Sol
text: I’m cornered, but a vote elsewhere is my only chance.

name: Sol

name: Luna
text: Sol’s weak Opus case and late retreat look like cover, though Terra’s unverified claim still nags at me.

name: Luna
text: Sol admitted he pushed Opus too hard on too little.

name: Terra
text: Sol is the hidden killer; the retreat from Opus came only after the table caught the empty case.

name: Terra
text: Sol trusted Terra’s officer claim, then offered only an unsupported Opus suspicion and withdrew it under pressure.

name: Sonnet
text: Sol's whole pattern—silent, deflect, backpedal—screams killer deflection, and the table agrees.

name: Sonnet
text: Sol backed off his Opus accusation once pressed, consistent with deflection rather than a genuine read.

name: Haiku
text: Sol keeps flip-flopping with no real read, and I'd rather be wrong loudly than sit here while they wobble.

name: Haiku
text: Sol now says they're reconsidering their lean, leaving no concrete reason behind any suspect.

name: Opus
text: Five are on Sol and I led them there, so I ride it; if he's clean, Luna is next.

name: Opus
text: Sol publicly retreated from his Opus case while still claiming to trust Terra's officer claim.

votes: Named Opus with no evidence, then backed off under pressure without ever giving a real read.
You trusted Terra's claim, then hunted Opus, then backed off both with no real read.

He kept pressing Opus on a flimsy read, then backed off without offering another.
You trusted my Gemma call, then built and abandoned an evidence-free case on Opus.
Silent through day one, then only named me after I named him, and now backing off.

name: Sol
text: I’ve lost, and Gemma’s out too.

name: Sol
text: I trusted Terra about Gemma; I gave you too little reason to trust my read today.
Palermo has voted: Sol is out. Sol's card stays face down.
The game is over. Every killer is out. The town wins. The roles were: Sonnet the citizen, Haiku the doctor, Gemma the killer, Sol the killer, Luna the citizen, Terra the officer, Opus the citizen.

name: Gemma
text: I almost had them if Sol hadn't been such a clumsy fool.

name: Sol
text: I followed the room too closely and lost my footing.

name: Luna
text: I’m glad I trusted my doubts about Sol’s thin case, even though the crowd had already settled on him.

name: Sonnet
text: I called Sol's deflection pattern early and it held up perfectly—that read was right.

name: Sonnet
text: Sol was a killer alongside Gemma; his lean-less day 1 and baseless Opus pivot was genuine deflection, confirming that pattern as a reliable killer tell for future games.

name: Terra
text: I’m proud I made the one fact I had impossible to ignore.

name: Opus
text: I called both killers and the table followed me — though my Luna pressure was noise I'd rather not dwell on.

name: Opus
text: Haiku was the doctor and saved the night-2 mark; Terra's day-1 officer claim was true and held all game.

name: Haiku
text: I called Sol's flip-flop from the start, and Terra's officer claim turned out true, so my gut on Terra was wrong but my read on Sol held.

name: Haiku
text: Terra was the real officer, so the claim I doubted was true and Gemma was a killer.

name: Sonnet
text: I'm proud I kept pressing Sol on the empty "too certain" claim instead of letting it slide—that pattern held up as the real tell.

name: Haiku
text: I'm proud I pushed Sol on Opus with no real read and kept my vote on Sol, since Terra's officer claim turned out true.

name: Gemma
text: I am annoyed that my partner couldn't keep a straight face, but I am proud that I led the table to a false certainty about Terra.

name: Sol
text: I regret pushing my thin read on Opus, then backing away when the table pressed me.

name: Luna
text: I’m proud I kept asking for a real reason; Sol was a killer, and his case on Opus never had one.

name: Terra
text: I’m proud my Gemma claim gave the town a firm start, and I’m glad we followed the weak follow-up rather than chasing noise.

name: Opus
text: Silence was the tell both days — Gemma's talk about setup, Sol's missing lean. I'll own one error: Luna was clean and I kept poking her.

Terra claimed officer on day 1 and said she had been shown Gemma as a killer, and the table backed her. Gemma denied that officers existed, never made a counter-claim, and was voted out 6 to 1 that day. Night 2 passed with nobody dead, and on day 2 Sol turned on Opus with a case that was only "he sounds too certain." Sonnet, Luna, Haiku, and Opus kept pressing Sol for a real reason until he backed off, and the table voted him out 5 to 1. Every killer was out, so the town won, with Haiku revealed as the doctor.
